_purpose: Functional scenarios (1 success + technique-driven alternative[]) per acceptance criterion for UC2 (Live Stream Pause State). No unit tests. Executable-ready.
_status: phase-3-3 output — 2026-07-09. Derived from PDT-3563-uc2-complete-jira-story.json (AC+BR) + PDT-3563-uc2-test-design.md (L3 conditions).

_rules_applied.split_per_state: None — no UC2 AC has >1 valid outcome by entry play-state (AC-03's ended-vs-recorded is a data variation, carried as an alternative, not a precondition-state split).
_rules_applied.one_owner_per_br: BR-01/BR-07/BR-09/BR-11 → SC-UC2-01 (the compound pause behaviour) · BR-13 → SC-UC2-02 · BR-12 → SC-UC2-03 · BR-02 → SC-UC2-05 · BR-14 → SC-UC2-07 · BR-10/BR-15 → SC-UC2-08. Dependents cite (not re-test): resume/chat/no-frozen rules are asserted once in their owner.

scenarios.title: Pause a live stream — indicator, live chat, tap-outside dismiss, no seek
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: SDK room/stream state; web-Live overlay net-new (automate on web once built; iOS/Android now)
preconditions: watching a live stream at the live edge (Room status = live)
(mobile) controls overlay revealed per UC1 / (desktop) direct-tap pause available
steps: Pause via the central pause button
Assert: the central ▶ button overlay is shown as the pause indicator (no separate badge/banner)
Assert: chat keeps receiving new messages in real time
Tap outside the play button
Assert: the overlay dismisses and the stream stays paused (position unchanged, no seek)

expected.success: Pausing shows the central ▶ overlay as the pause indicator, chat keeps running live, and tapping outside the play button dismisses the overlay while the stream stays paused.
alternative: The Live pause overlay shows NO ±10s seek controls (seeking is not applicable to a Live stream — BR-01).
Tapping ON the play button resumes playback (distinct from the tap-outside dismiss).
There is no separate badge/banner — the ▶ overlay is the only pause-state indicator.

platform_expected.note: 2-step: first tap reveals controls (no pause); tapping the central button pauses (BR-09)

scenarios.title: Resume returns to the current live moment (not the paused position)
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: live source/player; assert ≈ live within tolerance NEVER exact (CONF-07). Short-pause tolerance feel per-platform = manual (TC-UC2-08b). ASSUME-buffer-tolerance is a PM QA-confirm, not a blocker.
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (chat kept running during the pause)
steps: Resume via the play button
Assert: playback seeks to the current live edge (position advances to ≈ live, not the paused offset)
Assert: the ▶ overlay dismisses
Assert: chat is uninterrupted (no missed/replayed messages)

expected.success: Resuming seeks to the current live edge (≈ live within normal buffering tolerance, never the paused position); the ▶ overlay dismisses and chat is uninterrupted.
alternative: Playback never resumes from the previous paused offset.
The resume target is asserted as 'near live within tolerance' — a few seconds behind live is expected, not exact-live (CONF-07).

scenarios.title: Stream ends while paused — terminal state wins, no frozen frame
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: flip SDK room.status; the simultaneous pause + host-end race (TC-UC2-07c) is staged manually
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream
steps: Mock: flip SDK room.status live → ended during the pause
Assert: the player leaves the paused state and shows the ended state (terminal wins)
Assert: the viewer is not left on a frozen frame (explicit ended feedback)

expected.success: When the room transitions to ended/recorded during a pause, the player leaves paused and shows the terminal state — the terminal state always wins over paused, and the viewer is never left on a frozen frame.
alternative: Recording not yet ready → 'Livestream ended' is shown, with NO intermediate 'processing' state.
Room becomes recorded → the player shows the recorded/VOD state.
A simultaneous pause + host-end race resolves to ended (terminal wins) — staged manually (TC-UC2-07c).

scenarios.title: Default — playing at the live edge before any pause
preconditions: a live stream (Room status = live) is playing at the live edge
the viewer has not yet paused
steps: Render the live player at the live edge without pausing
Assert: no ▶ pause indicator is present
Assert: the LIVE badge + viewer count render as-is; chat is live

expected.success: Before any pause, no pause indicator is shown; the LIVE badge and viewer count render as-is (unaffected by this feature) and chat is live.

scenarios.title: Mobile web has no pause control on Live
preconditions: a viewer on mobile web watching a Live stream
steps: Render the Live player in a mobile-web viewport
Assert: no pause control is offered (no pause affordance in the player chrome)

expected.success: On mobile web, a live stream offers no pause control — pause/resume of an active Live stream is not available on web-mobile (standing platform boundary, not a bug).
alternative: On web-desktop the pause control IS present (1-step pause).
On iOS / Android the pause control IS present (2-step reveal-then-pause).

scenarios.title: Long pause still resumes to the current live moment
scenarios.automation_note: manual: a long real pause on a real broadcast (TC-UC2-08c) — the automatable resume-to-live core is covered by SC-UC2-02
preconditions: the user paused a live stream for an extended period (minutes)
steps: Pause for several minutes on a real broadcast
Resume
Assert: playback snaps to the current live moment; a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable

expected.success: After a long pause, resuming snaps to the current live moment regardless of the jump size — a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable while it catches up.
alternative: The size of the jump does not change the guarantee — it never resumes from the paused position.
Resume lands ≈ live within tolerance (further behind after a long pause is still within the guarantee).

scenarios.title: Chat and video re-sync on resume — no replay, no skip
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: chat subscription; smoke-check on a real live feed at least once
preconditions: the user paused for a while (chat kept running live throughout)
steps: Capture chat message ids before resume
Resume
Capture chat message ids after resume
Assert: no message is replayed (duplicate) and none is skipped (gap); chat is aligned at the live moment

expected.success: On resume, chat and video are aligned at the live moment — no chat messages are replayed and none are skipped.
alternative: Comparing message ids before vs after resume shows no duplicate (replay) and no gap (skip).
After a long paused window with continuous chat, on resume chat is already at the live moment and aligns with the video.

scenarios.title: Network drops while paused — Reconnecting, stays paused, resume to live
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: network layer + SDK; iOS NWPathMonitor overlay-while-paused confirmed on a real device first (TC-UC2-10a)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream
steps: Mock: drop the network connection while paused
Assert: a 'Reconnecting' indicator (auto-retry, no manual button) is shown — not a no-feedback frozen frame
Mock: recover the network
Assert: the stream stays paused (no auto-resume)
Resume
Assert: playback snaps to the current live edge (≈ live within tolerance)

expected.success: A network drop while paused shows a 'Reconnecting' indicator (auto-retry, no manual button); the stream stays paused through drop→recover (no auto-resume); on user resume it snaps to the current live edge.
alternative: The stream never auto-resumes on network recover — it stays paused until the user explicitly resumes (no implicit toggle).
(iOS) the 'Reconnecting' scrim shows even while paused (device network via NWPathMonitor).
(web) a plain paused-video drop shows no overlay; only SDK room.status = 'waitingReconnect' (broadcaster drop) surfaces it.
